checks.title: kube-apiserver has --anonymous-auth=false
checks.rationale: Anonymous requests against the API server bypass authentication entirely.
checks.remediation: Add --anonymous-auth=false to kube-apiserver flags or 'anonymous: enabled: false' in config.

checks.title: kube-apiserver authorization-mode does not include AlwaysAllow
checks.rationale: AlwaysAllow disables authorization entirely; production should use Node,RBAC.

checks.title: kube-apiserver --audit-log-path is set
checks.rationale: API audit logging is required for forensic investigation and compliance.

checks.title: kube-apiserver --tls-cert-file and --client-ca-file are set
checks.command: ps -ef | grep '[k]ube-apiserver' | grep -qE -- '--tls-cert-file' && ps -ef | grep '[k]ube-apiserver' | grep -qE -- '--client-ca-file' && echo true || echo false
checks.rationale: Without TLS + client CA, the API is exposed in clear text and accepts any client.

checks.title: etcd has --client-cert-auth=true
checks.rationale: etcd holds the entire cluster state including Secrets - it must require client certs.

checks.title: etcd has --peer-client-cert-auth=true
checks.rationale: Peer-cert auth prevents unauthorized etcd nodes from joining the cluster.

checks.title: kubelet --anonymous-auth=false
checks.rationale: Anonymous kubelet access exposes node-level container actions.

checks.title: kubelet --authorization-mode=Webhook
checks.rationale: Webhook authz delegates kubelet decisions to the API server's RBAC.

checks.title: kubelet --read-only-port=0
checks.rationale: The read-only port exposes pod/node metadata without authentication.

checks.title: Manual: pods admission policy in use (Pod Security Standards / OPA / Kyverno)
checks.audit: kubectl get ns -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}{"\t"}{.metadata.labels.pod-security\\.kubernetes\\.io/enforce}{"\n"}{end}'. Confirm production namespaces enforce 'restricted' or 'baseline'.
checks.rationale: Without an admission policy, pods can run privileged, host-network, hostPID, etc.

checks.title: Manual: NetworkPolicies are defined for production namespaces
checks.audit: Run 'kubectl get netpol -A'. Confirm a default-deny NetworkPolicy exists in each production namespace.
checks.rationale: Without NetworkPolicies, pods accept traffic from any source.
checks.remediation: Apply default-deny + explicit allow NetworkPolicies per namespace.

checks.title: Manual: Kubernetes Secrets are encrypted at rest
checks.audit: Inspect --encryption-provider-config on kube-apiserver. Confirm aescbc or kms is configured (not 'identity').
checks.rationale: By default etcd stores Secrets in base64-only form (not encrypted).
checks.remediation: Configure EncryptionConfiguration with kms (cloud KMS) or aescbc.

checks.title: kube-apiserver does not use --basic-auth-file
checks.command: ps -ef | grep '[k]ube-apiserver' | grep -qE -- '--basic-auth-file' && echo present || echo absent
checks.rationale: Static basic-auth files are an insecure, deprecated authentication method.
checks.remediation: Remove --basic-auth-file and use OIDC or client certificates.

checks.title: kube-apiserver does not use --token-auth-file
checks.command: ps -ef | grep '[k]ube-apiserver' | grep -qE -- '--token-auth-file' && echo present || echo absent
checks.rationale: Static token files are long-lived bearer credentials that cannot be revoked easily.
checks.remediation: Remove --token-auth-file; use short-lived ServiceAccount tokens or OIDC.

checks.title: kube-apiserver has --profiling=false
checks.command: ps -ef | grep '[k]ube-apiserver' | grep -qE -- '--profiling=false' && echo set || echo unset
checks.rationale: Profiling endpoints expose detailed system/program information.

checks.title: kube-apiserver has --service-account-lookup=true
checks.command: ps -ef | grep '[k]ube-apiserver' | grep -qE -- '--service-account-lookup=true' && echo set || echo unset
checks.rationale: Validates that the ServiceAccount token still exists in etcd, enabling revocation.

checks.title: kube-apiserver verifies the kubelet certificate authority
checks.command: ps -ef | grep '[k]ube-apiserver' | grep -qE -- '--kubelet-certificate-authority' && echo set || echo unset
checks.rationale: Without a kubelet CA, the API server cannot verify kubelet identity (MITM risk).
checks.remediation: Set --kubelet-certificate-authority to the cluster CA bundle.

checks.title: kube-apiserver audit log retention is 30 days or more
checks.rationale: Sufficient audit retention is required for incident investigation.

checks.title: etcd does not enable --auto-tls
checks.command: ps -ef | grep '[e]tcd' | grep -qE -- '--auto-tls=true' && echo enabled || echo disabled
checks.rationale: Auto-TLS uses self-signed certs that defeat client identity verification.
checks.remediation: Remove --auto-tls=true; provide explicit etcd server certificates.

checks.title: kube-controller-manager binds to localhost only
checks.rationale: Binding to localhost prevents remote access to the controller-manager port.

checks.title: kube-controller-manager has --profiling=false
checks.command: ps -ef | grep '[k]ube-controller-manager' | grep -qE -- '--profiling=false' && echo set || echo unset
checks.rationale: Profiling endpoints expose internal program data.

checks.title: kube-controller-manager uses individual service-account credentials
checks.command: ps -ef | grep '[k]ube-controller-manager' | grep -qE -- '--use-service-account-credentials=true' && echo set || echo unset
checks.rationale: Separate SA credentials per controller enable least privilege via RBAC.

checks.title: kube-scheduler binds to localhost only
checks.rationale: Binding to localhost prevents remote access to the scheduler port.

checks.title: kube-apiserver static pod manifest is 600 or stricter
checks.rationale: World-writable manifests let an attacker alter control-plane flags.

checks.title: admin.conf kubeconfig is 600 or stricter
checks.rationale: admin.conf grants cluster-admin; it must not be readable by other users.
